headline: GOLDGROUP-GORO CLOSES TONIGHT — $372M Mexico Gold Merger Creates Multi-Mine NYSE Producer; Trading Monday Under GORO
snippet: Goldgroup Mining (TSX: GGAZF) and Gold Resource Corporation (NYSE: GORO) are completing their US$372 million merger after market close tonight, July 17, following BC Supreme Court final approval and a 99.99% shareholder vote in favor — creating a new multi-mine Mexico-focused precious metals producer spanning the Cerro Prieto mine and San Francisco project in Sonora, the Don David mine in Oaxaca, and the Back Forty project in Michigan. The combined company will commence trading under the GORO ticker on NYSE American starting July 20 after Goldgroup completes its 4:1 share consolidation, marking a graduation from TSX-V to a major U.S. exchange.

headline: VIZSLA THIRA PORPHYRY: 472m at 0.40% CuEq — 304.8m Sub-Interval at 0.48%; Phase 2 Starting Weeks, Central B.C. (TSXV:VCU)
snippet: Vizsla Copper (TSX-V: VCU) reported final results from its spring Phase 1 drill program at the Thira porphyry discovery in central British Columbia, with standout hole TH26-154 returning 472.8 metres at 0.40% copper equivalent including 304.8 metres at 0.48% CuEq — its widest, highest-grade copper interval to date from this emerging bulk-tonnage porphyry system. The 21-hole Phase 1 program totaled over 11,200 metres across the Thira Discovery, Camp Lake, and Copper Pond targets; Phase 2 drilling is set to begin within weeks focusing on structural offsets to the Thira Discovery and the southern extent of copper-molybdenum-silver mineralization.

headline: PERSEUS YAOURÉ OUTPERFORMING BY 24% — +24% Metal Above Reserve Model in Open Pit; $34M FY27 Drill Budget; CMA Underground Now Producing (ASX/TSX:PRU)
snippet: Perseus Mining (ASX/TSX: PRU) disclosed that its Yaouré open pit in Côte d'Ivoire has identified 24% more metal than the reserve model over the six months to March 2026, as ongoing resource definition drilling defines additional mineralisation domains and confirms down-dip and along-strike extensions that support a longer mine life. The company committed A$34 million to drilling in FY27 to convert Inferred Resources and grow the Mineral Resource base, while the CMA underground operation — cleared by the President of Côte d'Ivoire — is transitioning to production with a second jumbo to be mobilised to increase ore delivery.

headline: FOUNDERS ANTINO NORTHEAST CONFIRMED — New Discovery Returns 58.5m at 1.00 g/t Au; 4 Active Gold Systems in 70,000m Suriname Campaign (TSXV:FDR)
snippet: Founders Metals (TSX-V: FDR) confirmed a new Antino Northeast discovery in its mid-year update from the fully funded 70,000-metre Antino Gold Project in southeastern Suriname, with discovery hole ANE009 returning 58.5 metres at 1.00 g/t Au from 18.6 metres and a second hole 1,200 metres away hitting 53.0 metres at 0.46 g/t Au — demonstrating the scale of the NE system. The H1 2026 update also shows continued high-grade results from Antino West (53.1m at 1.21 g/t Au from surface) and the Froyo Zone (9.0m at 12.21 g/t Au within 37.0m at 3.27 g/t Au), making Antino one of the more active multi-system junior gold campaigns in the Americas.

headline: GALLEON GOLD ZONE #9 REACHES 500m VERTICAL — Down-Dip Continuity Confirmed 360m Below Stopes; South Zone Footprint Also Expanding (TSXV:GGO)
snippet: Galleon Gold (TSX-V: GGO) confirmed the down-dip continuity of its Zone #9 high-grade gold system at the West Cache Gold Project in Timmins, Ontario, with new 2026 holes extending mineralisation 360 metres further down-plunge from the planned bulk-sample stopes to a vertical depth of 500 metres below surface — deepening a system that previously delivered 16.07 g/t Au over 9.25m within a broader 4.07 g/t Au over 40.9m interval at 440m depth. The announcement also reports the South Zone's expanding footprint, adding to the project's overall resource potential within this 18,000-metre 2026 program in one of Canada's historic gold districts.

headline: SILVER DROPS 1.4% TODAY, GOLD HOLDS — Ratio Pierces 70:1 Near Historic High; Sixth Consecutive Supply Deficit of 46M oz Now Confirmed
snippet: Silver fell 1.4% Thursday after June U.S. retail sales beat expectations — reviving Fed rate hike bets and pressuring the industrial metal harder than gold — driving the gold-silver ratio to approximately 70:1, near the high end of its modern 50-year historical range, according to GoldSilver.com's market commentary. The ratio had compressed to 55:1 as recently as May 2026; the Silver Institute's World Silver Survey 2026 confirms the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit at 46.3 million ounces, a structural tightness that remains in tension with the short-term macro headwind from elevated real yields.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD MUST BREAK $4,260 BY AUGUST — Or Risks Leg Down; $3,830 Is the Line; $4,550+ Possible If It Holds
snippet: GoldSeek's Asian Metals Market Update for July 15, 2026 identified $4,260 as the critical near-term threshold for gold: a decisive break above that level by the first week of August opens the path to $4,550+, while failure to do so — or a close below $3,830 — would signal a deeper corrective leg. The analysis notes that gold has spent much of H1 2026 consolidating after January's $5,589 record, with silver's dual industrial-monetary demand profile currently the swing variable as markets price a meaningful probability of another Federal Reserve rate hike driven by stubborn Middle East-linked inflation.

headline: CHILE COPPER CRASHES 13% — Escondida -17.6%, Codelco -18.3%, Collahuasi -19.3% in May; July Atmospheric River Adds Fresh Disruption
snippet: Chile's copper output fell 12.94% year-on-year to 423,623 metric tonnes in May 2026, with simultaneous sharp declines at all three major producers — BHP Escondida -17.6%, Codelco -18.3%, Collahuasi -19.3% — driven by structural ore grade deterioration, Atacama water constraints, and operational disruptions at El Teniente following a 2025 fatal incident. An atmospheric river event sweeping Chile's copper-producing regions in July has since forced emergency ministerial meetings and temporary mine suspensions, tightening supply further even as copper futures recover above $6.26–$6.30 per pound on the CME.

headline: LITHIUM HITS 4-MONTH LOW — CATL Jianxiawo Safety Permit Renewed, Bald Hill and Finniss Also Restarting; CNY 151,000/t Sliding
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices fell to CNY 151,000 per tonne — a four-month low — as CATL received a renewed safety permit for its Jianxiawo mine in China, returning approximately 46,000 metric tonnes LCE of annual production capacity to an already-oversupplied spot market. Mineral Resources' Bald Hill lithium mine in Western Australia is also set to restart after an 18-month suspension and Core Lithium's Finniss project is similarly resuming, amplifying supply pressure at a moment when global EV sales growth has slowed sharply to approximately 0.9% year-to-date, according to industry data.

headline: VANECK: MINING STOCKS UP 46%, STILL AT A DISCOUNT — Imaru Casanova Says $4,000 Pullback Is 'Noise'; Q2 Earnings Could Reprice Sector
snippet: VanEck portfolio manager Imaru Casanova told Kitco News that the current pullback in gold toward $4,000 is "noise" in a structural bull market, noting that gold mining equities have outperformed the S&P 500 by a factor of two in 2026 (up 46% vs. 22%) while all-in sustaining costs average below $2,000/oz — leaving margins robust even at $4,000 gold. Casanova argued that institutional investors remain significantly underexposed to the sector, consensus sell-side estimates are below current realized gold prices, and Q2 2026 earnings season beginning in late July could catalyse a meaningful re-rating as record cash flows and balance sheet strength are reported.
